title: How Many Prime Factors Could a Counterexample to Giuga's Conjecture Have?
description: Lean 4 (v4.35.0) + Mathlib formalization of structural theorems, edge-dual linear-programming relaxations (Lemma W and refinements), Lemma C, local obstruction rules, unconditional counterexample lower bounds, explicit ceiling witnesses, and conditional transfer theorems for Giuga's conjecture. Across 21 compared theorems (zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only), Lean 4 proves unconditionally that every Giuga counterexample has at least 578 distinct prime factors and exceeds 10^1803 (>= 1,804 decimal digits), constructs an explicit 8,135-prime normal odd prime set (40,733 digits) and an explicit 8,138-prime witness satisfying all seven local counterexample rules (40,751 digits), proves Lemma W, Lemma C, and the mod-8 factor-count congruence, and proves conditional transfer theorems reaching >= 8,138 prime factors and > 10^40747 (>= 40,748 decimal digits) from explicit depth-6 frontier certificate hypotheses.
